scientific_objective: Determine whether an alternative segmentation loss improves regional-refiner crop segmentation quality, boundary fidelity, or small/tiny stone detection behavior compared to the Phase-14 baseline loss, while strictly isolating loss formulation as the sole independent variable across identical architecture, data splits, crop geometry, and optimization schedules.
research_question: Can an alternative segmentation loss improve regional-refiner crop quality or object-size behavior without degrading overall full-field pipeline performance, when keeping architecture, dataset, crop geometry, optimizer, and training protocol fixed?

experimental_control.name: BCE_Dice_Balanced
experimental_control.mathematical_definition: L_{BCE} = - \frac{1}{N} \sum [y \log \sigma(z) + (1-y) \log (1-\sigma(z))]; L_{Dice} = 1 - \frac{2 \sum \sigma(z) y + \epsilon}{\sum \sigma(z) + \sum y + \epsilon}; L_0 = 0.5 L_{BCE} + 0.5 L_{Dice}
experimental_control.retraining_policy: L0 will NOT be retrained. Pre-training verification confirmed that the Phase-15 L0 implementation achieves exact numerical equivalence to the frozen Phase-14 implementation on fixed tensors.

candidate_loss_suite.name: Focal_Dice

verified_alpha_semantics.positive_pixel_weight: alpha_t = alpha = 0.25 on foreground stone pixels (y=1)
verified_alpha_semantics.negative_pixel_weight: alpha_t = 1 - alpha = 0.75 on background tissue pixels (y=0)

candidate_loss_suite.corrected_rationale: In regional radiograph crops, background tissue constitutes the vast majority of pixels. Alpha=0.25 (with 1-alpha=0.75 on background) combines with the focal modulating factor (1-p_t)^2.0 to heavily suppress loss contributions from confident, easy background pixels while penalizing false-positive background tissue, focusing parameter updates onto ambiguous anatomical borders and difficult stone/background pixels. This potentially reduces FALSE REGIONAL FOREGROUND within predicted proposal crops. It does NOT modify proposal count, proposal geometry, Stage-4D localization, NMS, or TopK (which remain strictly frozen).

candidate_loss_suite.mathematical_definition: p_t = y \sigma(z) + (1-y) (1-\sigma(z)); \alpha_t = y \alpha + (1-y) (1-\alpha); L_{Focal} = - \alpha_t (1 - p_t)^\gamma \log(p_t); L_{Dice} = 1 - \frac{2 \sum \sigma(z) y + \epsilon}{\sum \sigma(z) + \sum y + \epsilon}; L_1 = 0.5 L_{Focal} + 0.5 L_{Dice}

constants.background_handling: smooth weighting via (1 - p_t)^gamma and alpha_t

candidate_loss_suite.name: Tversky_Loss

verified_weights_convention.convention_status: VERIFIED_CORRECT (beta=0.70 > alpha=0.30 prioritizes stone recall over precision)

candidate_loss_suite.rationale: Inside 256x256 regional crops, Tiny and Small stones occupy a minute fraction (< 0.1%) of foreground pixels. Asymmetric Tversky penalization weights False Negatives more heavily than False Positives (beta=0.70 vs alpha=0.30), directly penalizing missed stone boundaries and boosting small-target sensitivity without post-hoc threshold shifting.
candidate_loss_suite.mathematical_definition: TP = \sum \sigma(z) y; FP = \sum \sigma(z) (1-y); FN = \sum (1-\sigma(z)) y; TI = \frac{TP + \epsilon}{TP + \alpha FP + \beta FN + \epsilon}; L_2 = 1.0 - TI

constants.sigmoid_placement: applied internally to logits before overlap summation
constants.batch_aggregation: per-crop Tversky Index averaged across batch

candidate_loss_suite.name: Focal_Tversky_Loss
candidate_loss_suite.family: Non-linear Tversky Reshaping with High-Overlap Sensitivity

mathematical_gradient_derivation.autograd_agreement: PASS (Verified to < 1e-10 difference against PyTorch autograd across all TI test points)
mathematical_gradient_derivation.mathematical_interpretation: Because gamma = 0.75 < 1 in L = (1 - TI)^gamma, the magnitude of dL/dTI increases as TI approaches 1 (from 0.750 at TI=0.00 to 2.372 at TI=0.99). Therefore, this formulation emphasizes incremental refinement in the high-overlap regime relative to standard Tversky loss, rather than preferentially amplifying the gradient when TI << 1.

candidate_loss_suite.corrected_rationale: The gamma=0.75 transformation nonlinearly reshapes Tversky loss so that sensitivity with respect to TI increases as overlap approaches 1, while the alpha=0.30 / beta=0.70 Tversky term retains FN-heavy recall weighting.
candidate_loss_suite.parameter_justification: gamma=0.75 is scientifically defensible and retained under this exact formula because it establishes a unique high-overlap sensitivity distinct from linear Tversky (L2) and pixel-wise focal suppression (L1).

constants.sigmoid_placement: applied internally to logits before overlap summation
constants.batch_aggregation: per-crop Focal Tversky averaged across batch

negative_crop_behavior_audit.context: A3 training inventory contains 1542 pure background negative crops (target mask has zero foreground pixels).

findings_by_loss.L0_BCE_Dice: BCE term provides active, non-zero gradient (norm ~0.0275) penalizing any predicted false-positive foreground. Dice term evaluates to 1.0 with zero gradient. Combined L0 effectively trains suppression on negative crops via BCE.
findings_by_loss.L1_Focal_Dice: Focal term provides active, non-zero gradient (norm ~0.0252) penalizing false-positive pixels with alpha_t = 0.75 and (1 - p_t)^2.0. Dice term evaluates to 1.0 with zero gradient. Combined L1 actively trains background suppression on negative crops.
findings_by_loss.L2_Tversky: When target is pure zero, TP=0 and FN=0. TI = epsilon / (alpha * FP + epsilon). Because epsilon=1e-6 << alpha * FP, TI evaluates to ~0.0 and Tversky loss evaluates to 1.0 - 1e-8 ~ 1.000000 with near-zero gradient (norm ~1e-9). Pure overlap Tversky produces effectively zero gradient on completely empty targets.
findings_by_loss.L3_Focal_Tversky: Inherits L2 behavior: on pure zero targets, (1 - TI)^0.75 evaluates to ~1.0 with near-zero gradient (norm ~1e-9).

negative_crop_behavior_audit.scientific_assessment: This asymmetry is an inherent, mathematically authentic property of pure overlap losses (Dice/Tversky) versus compound distribution+overlap losses (BCE+Dice, Focal+Dice). In A3 training, negative crops are batched alongside positive crops (batch size 8). For L2 and L3, negative crops act as passive non-interfering distractors, whereas L0 and L1 actively backpropagate background suppression. This constitutes a fundamental scientific comparison between compound losses and pure asymmetric overlap losses in Phase 15. No artificial hacks or code modifications will be introduced; the comparison reflects authentic loss behavior.
